correctness.rationale: Any nonempty intersecting 3-uniform hypergraph with every active pair contained in at least three triples must be K_5^(3) on its active support, possibly with isolates. The submitted finite triple-pair propagation proof has the right conditions and boundary: one triple forces additional triple choices; intersecting constraints force support into five vertices and δ₂⁺≥3 then forces each active pair to have all its three completions. Independently, Spiro’s 2021 structural result (Proposition 2.11 plus Lemma 2.5 for r=k-s+t=3,k=3,s=t=1) implies containment in all 10 triples of a five-set; closure under pair completions forces all ten triples. All 1023 nonempty 3-graphs on five labeled vertices were also enumerated; only K5³ met the conditions. The actual all-n proof rests on structural reasoning, not this finite check.

originality.rationale: The entire assertion is implied by Sam Spiro’s 2021 preprint / 2023 SIAM paper. Its unrestricted Proposition 2.11 rules out bad triples for t-intersecting r-graphs with δ_{r-s}⁺>binom(k−1,s); Lemma 2.5 then forces containment in a (2k−2s+t,k−s+t)-kernel system when r=k−s+t. At (k,r,s,t)=(3,3,1,1), this is containment in a complete 3-uniform hypergraph on five vertices. Since every active pair has codegree at least three and there are exactly three possible completions within five vertices, starting from any triple and closing under the connected Johnson graph J(5,3) forces all ten triples. The prior theorem is not limited to maximum-size H in this special case: the paper explicitly says the containment conclusion holds regardless of |H|. The proposed complete rigidity classification is thus a direct special-case corollary, not an original research result.

value.rationale: The positive pair-codegree rigidity statement is a natural combinatorial fact, but its complete assertion is a short forced specialization of the already-published size-independent kernel containment theorem of Spiro. The only additional step is immediate closure under all three pair completions in K5³. As a proposed independent mathematical research contribution it is a routine known-theorem corollary, not a motivated unresolved gap or substantive new classification; correctness alone cannot supply value.
